questions.text: According to lesson 3, how is the appropriate position size calculated for a trade?
options: Multiply total capital by the stop-loss percentage
Divide the amount you are willing to lose by the stop-loss distance
Set position size equal to the total capital
Use the average volume of the asset as the size
questions.explanation: Position size equals the risk amount divided by the stop-loss distance to keep risk per trade within limits.

questions.text: True or false: Reviewing a trade journal weekly helps traders spot patterns such as exiting too early or over-trading after a win and adjust their risk parameters accordingly.
questions.explanation: The weekly journal review serves as a feedback loop that informs adjustments to risk or stop‑loss placement.

questions.text: What is the core idea of range trading as explained in lesson 2?
options: Buying only when price makes new highs
Placing automated orders to buy near support and sell near resistance to profit from normal volatility
Avoiding any use of stop‑loss orders
Relying solely on news events to time entries
questions.explanation: Range trading exploits predictable price oscillations between support and resistance without needing to forecast news.

questions.text: True or false: Extremely positive funding rates on perpetual futures suggest that most traders are leveraged long, which can signal an overheated market prone to a sharp pullback.
questions.explanation: High positive funding rates indicate crowded long positions, often preceding a market correction.
